answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can pay only for marginal uniqueness. Each finished task is hashed into an embedding commitment, and the ledger computes its delta against all previously attested outputs: a tiny delta means the result merely mirrors an existing solution, so the work is rejected and its fee burned. Peers verify these comparisons against the crystal-clear on-chain commitments, so duplicates cannot slip past review. Each clone must genuinely solve a distinct task to earn: N identities cost N times the compute and fees yet add zero reward, making cloning strictly loss-making.
